segments.title:
Bilboes
gold project
segments.say: A 600 million dollar gold mine is being built in Zimbabwe, and the Victoria Falls Stock Exchange helped pay for it. Here's the breakdown.

segments.title: The mine
segments.source: Project figures as announced (Mining Zimbabwe) · first-gold date confirmed by Proactive Investors
segments.say: Caledonia Mining's Bilboes project plans to produce about 1.55 million ounces of gold over eleven years. First gold is targeted for October 2028, with 500 permanent jobs.

segments.title: Who paid for it
segments.source: Proactive Investors (5 Nov 2026) · Caledonia CEO interview
segments.say: The money: 150 million dollars from eight Zimbabwean banks, led by Stanbic and CBZ, and 150 million raised in New York. Caledonia also raised equity on the VFEX.

segments.title: What it could pay
segments.source: Project projections as announced, assuming US$4,000/oz gold (Mining Zimbabwe)
segments.say: At a gold price of 4,000 dollars an ounce, the project says it could bring in over 6 billion dollars of foreign currency, 975 million in corporate tax and 300 million in royalties. These are projections, not guarantees.
But what is the VFEX, anyway?

segments.title: The VFEX in brief
segments.say: The Victoria Falls Stock Exchange trades in US dollars, not ZiG, and charges no capital gains tax on listed shares. Fifteen counters are on its price list.

segments.title: VFEX this year
segments.sub: Year-to-date share price change to 19 Nov
segments.say: This year, Zimplow and Padenga have more than doubled. Caledonia itself is down about 22 percent year to date, while it spends heavily on Bilboes.

lines: Long-term project finance: the final funding step
Gold price: the projections assume US$4,000/oz

segments.say: Watch for the final long-term funding deal, and the gold price, because every projection depends on it. Not financial advice. Follow for more.
